entries.title: Ask can rank review submissions by score and delete Live Transcribe recordings
entries.summary: Two new tools expand what **Ask** can do. **Get review scores** ranks a Review plan's submissions by score, with filters for round, category and stage, a configurable sort and limit, and a per-reviewer outstanding tally — using the same data as the Submissions directory tab and export. **Delete live capture recording** removes a Live Transcribe transcript (with a confirmation that names the session by title); a companion **List live capture recordings** tool lets Ask find the right recording first.
entries.use_case: An organizer can ask Ask to show the top-scoring submissions in a review round — filtered by category or stage — without opening the Submissions directory. They can also ask Ask to delete a Live Transcribe recording for a named session when a capture needs to be removed after the event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to quickly surface top-scoring submissions from a review round, or when they need to remove a Live Transcribe recording and want to do it through Ask.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Review plans (especially multi-round or multi-category programs) and customers using Live Transcribe who manage post-event recordings.
internal.staff_path: Ask (Agent window) — type a question about review scores or live capture recordings
internal.gotchas: Delete live capture recording is destructive and hard-deletes the transcript rows; the session record and any uploaded media files are not affected. Ask requires the user to confirm the session title before deleting. get_review_scores pages up to 200 submissions per call and ranks using existing scoring data — no new scoring logic is introduced.
internal.talk_track: You can now ask Ask things like 'Show me the top 20 submissions in round 2 of my review plan, sorted by score' or 'Delete the live capture recording for the session titled X' — Ask will confirm the session name before removing anything.

draft.docs_gap: The Ask / Agent window guide should add a section listing the review-scores and live-capture-recording tools, including the filters available (round, category, stage, sort, limit) and the confirmation behaviour on the destructive delete action.
draft.why_use_it: Ask lets you query and act on your event data in plain language from the Agent window, without navigating to individual module pages. Use it to get quick answers about review scores, speaker readiness, agenda gaps, or live-capture recordings — and to take actions like deleting a transcript — all in one conversation.

entries.title: Admins and agents can add a nomination on someone's behalf
entries.summary: Admins and AI agents can now submit a nomination for any nominee without waiting for the nomination window to be open. Send a request with the nominee's email, optional name and organisation details, a category, and form answers; the API returns the entry status, any **missing_fields** still needed, and a direct URL to the draft. Calling again with the same nominee email reuses the existing draft rather than creating a duplicate. The same capability is available through the Public API and the Sessionboard MCP connector (`add_awards_nomination`).
entries.use_case: An awards team that wants to seed nominations from a curated list — or let an AI agent rehearse the review workflow on a test program — can add entries directly without asking nominees to submit themselves, even when the nomination window is closed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to add nominations from an internal list, backfill entries from a previous system, or let an AI agent test an awards program end-to-end.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running Awards who needs to enter nominations on behalf of nominees or automate nomination intake via the Public API or MCP.
internal.gotchas: Staff entry bypasses the nomination-window check, so drafts can be created even on closed or draft programs. No confirmation email is sent to the nominee or nominator — remind customers to handle nominee communication separately. Calling the endpoint again with the same nominee email reuses the existing draft rather than creating a new one.
internal.talk_track: If you have a list of people you want to nominate — from a spreadsheet, your CRM, or a previous year's program — you can now push them straight into your awards program through the API or by asking your AI assistant, without opening nominations to the public.

draft.docs_gap: The managing-submissions guide should add a section explaining how admins and agents can add a nomination on someone's behalf (via the workspace API or MCP connector), including the nominee/nominator fields, how missing_fields works, and the idempotent draft behaviour.
draft.why_use_it: Managing submissions gives your team a single place to track every nomination from receipt through judging to winner selection. You can add entries on a nominee's behalf, assign reviewers, run multiple scoring rounds, and apply winner tags — all without nominees needing to interact with the form themselves. Use it when you want tighter control over what enters the pipeline or when you are seeding a program from an existing list of candidates.
